items.notes: 2026-07-16T18:36Z queue-drain-hourly: FIRST verification. REFUTED - closing as a false positive. Claim (1) HOLDS: .github/workflows/security.yml:49 does run `pnpm audit --audit-level=high --prod`. Claim (2) DOES NOT REPRODUCE and is the finding's whole premise: ran the exact command on the same repo (HEAD ba2ae66, tree clean, pnpm 9.15.0, node 22.22.2) and it exits 0 with "No known vulnerabilities found"; `pnpm audit --json --prod` returns a well-formed live advisory response (132 deps scanned, 0 vulns), not an error. Also does not reproduce at --audit-level=moderate, which the finding said failed identically. Probed the registry directly: the legacy quick-audit endpoint POST /-/npm/v1/security/audits/quick returns HTTP 200, not the claimed 410 "endpoint is being retired". So the endpoint the finding says was retired is live, and ERR_PNPM_AUDIT_BAD_RESPONSE does not occur. Claim (3) is built on a wrong inference: the finding reads "no security run since the green 2026-07-13T10:58Z one" as proof the job started failing. `gh run list --workflow=security.yml` shows 12/12 recent runs SUCCESS and zero failures. The real reason nothing has run since 07-13 is that main is 7 commits AHEAD of origin/main and unpushed, so no push ever triggered CI; the Monday 08:00 UTC cron last fired 07-13 (a Monday) and is not due again until 07-20. Most likely a transient npm registry incident during the bar-raise window, mis-generalised into a permanent endpoint retirement. items.evidence: scripts/push-to-github.ps1:74-82; scripts/git-guard.ps1:55
items.title: Capture $pushExit immediately after git push so Confirm-GitIntact cannot mask a rejected push
items.prompt: YaB MED (bar-raise 2026-07-10): push-to-github.ps1:74-82 runs `git push`, then `Confirm-GitIntact`, then tests `$LASTEXITCODE`. Confirm-GitIntact (git-guard.ps1:55) itself runs `git rev-parse --verify HEAD`, which overwrites $LASTEXITCODE with its own exit 0. A rejected push therefore reports success, and release.ps1 proceeds to tag and post to Discord for a version that never reached origin. Fix: capture `$pushExit = $LASTEXITCODE` on the line immediately after `git push`, then call Confirm-GitIntact, then test `$pushExit`. While in this file, also delete the blind `Remove-Item -Force .git\index.lock` block at lines 28-32 (see bar-raise-2026-07-04-yab-push-blind-lock-delete); it runs ahead of the Assert-GitSafe call at line 56 that exists to handle exactly that race. Ship via scripts/release.ps1.
items.completionNote: Fixed push-to-github.ps1: capture $pushExit = $LASTEXITCODE immediately after git push, before Confirm-GitIntact (whose git rev-parse resets $LASTEXITCODE to 0), and gate the failure exit on $pushExit. Committed e896109 (local, unpushed; loop/release carries the push).

items.title: Gnosis handler says 'keep the answer inline' - shipped model is deletable KV answer cards + ^q qids
items.detail: X:\YesAndGnosis\CLAUDE.md:37 reads '[x] = answered (keep the answer inline)'. That is the exact inverse of the shipped model: web/build.mjs:1676-1695 strips inline answers out of question text into deletable KV answer cards ('Answers live in the answer store ... never smushed into the question text'), and each question ends with a stable ^qXXXXXXXX block-ref token that IS the qid (build.mjs:1661-1684; worker.js:168 validates ^[0-9a-f]{8}$). Solo-dev voice, no em dashes. Ships via X:\YesAndRing\scripts\release.ps1. EXPANDED 2026-07-10 by audit-ring-nightly (CANONICAL_AUDIT-2026-07-10.md). The same doc region carries three further stale claims; fix them in the SAME deliberate pass. (a) HIGHEST PRIORITY, new + actively misleading: CLAUDE.md line 25 states the /api/state endpoint 'is unauthenticated (closed-beta grade; cat results are public TICA data)'. That is FALSE. src/index.js handleStateGet (~:770) and handleStatePost (~:795) both call verifyUser(request, env) and return 401 unauthorized when it fails; verifyUser (~:725) requires an Authorization: Bearer token and validates it against Supabase /auth/v1/user. POST keys the blob by the VERIFIED identity so no client can write another user's state; GET enforces self-only reads with a 403 unless the caller is a super-admin performing an audited view-as. Rewrite that line to describe the real posture. Risk if left: a contributor trusts the doc and strips the verifyUser/403 checks as dead closed-beta scaffolding. (b) CLAUDE.md line 20 and PROJECT_SPEC.md lines 74-75 both say persistence is 'localStorage until the backend lands'. The backend landed: schedulePush mirrors LOCAL to POST /api/state, boot hydrates from GET /api/state. localStorage is now a cache in front of a server of record, not the system of record. (c) CLAUDE.md lines 24-25 describe state as KV-only (KV RATINGS, key u:<email>). Reality: handleStatePost dual-writes KV AND pgStateWrite (RLS Postgres); handleStateGet reads Postgres when env.STATE_READ == 'pg', with KV fallback + lazy backfill, and KV remains the view-as/sharing source and rollback path. The STATE_READ migration flag is documented nowhere in the canonical layer. Also note for the reframe: cat sharing is LIVE, not pending - /api/share/grant, /api/share/revoke, /api/share/by-me and /api/shared-cats are all routed and implemented. And PROJECT_SPEC.md now self-contradicts within three lines: line 24 already says 'Auth email OTP codes' while line 26 still says 'magic-link auth ... not yet the live path'.

items.detail: sitemap.xml is hand-maintained. Nothing under scripts/ or .github/ writes it, and the site standard does not name it as a step when a project card lands. Design pages stay out of the sitemap on purpose because they are client-gated. Not auto-fixed because it adds a build step or a release guard, which is a structural call. items.title: Rising has 32 untracked .uid files while 115 are tracked
items.detail: BrackishRising tracks 115 Godot .uid files but leaves 32 untracked, and .gitignore does not exclude them. The untracked ones all sit next to modules created during the god-file decomposition (unit_commander.gd.uid, grid_renderer.gd.uid, unit_collision.gd.uid and the rest). items.title: SECURITY-ASSESSMENT marks rate limiting "fixed" but srv_* RPCs bypass the Worker limiter entirely
items.detail: docs/SECURITY-ASSESSMENT-2026-07-01.md finding #3 ("No rate limiting or CAPTCHA on public write paths") is marked fixed, remediated by "Cloudflare Workers rate-limiting binding on all /api POSTs". But src/index.js:72 authenticates to Supabase with the ANON key and passes p_secret: env.WORKER_SECRET, so every srv_* function is anon-executable and reachable directly at ${SUPABASE_URL}/rest/v1/rpc/srv_mark_released using the publishable anon key that ships in wrangler.jsonc and public/config.js. That path never traverses the Worker, so the Worker rate limiter is not a control on the money-path RPCs. This is intentional and documented (0015 header comment) and srv_ok() compares a SHA-256 of the secret, so there is NO breach and no schema change wanted. The defect is documentation accuracy: the sole control on srv_mark_paid/released/refunded is WORKER_SECRET entropy, and the assessment implies a rate-limit coverage it does not have. Fix: amend finding #3 to scope the remediation to the Worker /api surface, and add an explicit accepted-risk entry for the PostgREST srv_* surface naming WORKER_SECRET as its control. Optionally consider whether the Worker should use a service_role key so srv_* EXECUTE can be revoked from anon/authenticated as real defense in depth.

items.notes: 2026-07-16T18:36Z queue-drain-hourly: FIRST verification. REFUTED - closing as a false positive. Claim (1) HOLDS: .github/workflows/security.yml:49 does run `pnpm audit --audit-level=high --prod`. Claim (2) DOES NOT REPRODUCE and is the finding's whole premise: ran the exact command on the same repo (HEAD ba2ae66, tree clean, pnpm 9.15.0, node 22.22.2) and it exits 0 with "No known vulnerabilities found"; `pnpm audit --json --prod` returns a well-formed live advisory response (132 deps scanned, 0 vulns), not an error. Probed the registry directly: the legacy quick-audit endpoint POST /-/npm/v1/security/audits/quick returns HTTP 200, not the claimed 410 "endpoint is being retired". So the endpoint the finding says was retired is live, and ERR_PNPM_AUDIT_BAD_RESPONSE does not occur. Claim (3) is built on a wrong inference: the finding reads "no security run since the green 2026-07-13T10:58Z one" as proof the job started failing. `gh run list --workflow=security.yml` shows 12/12 recent runs SUCCESS and zero failures. Most likely a transient npm registry incident during the bar-raise window, mis-generalised into a permanent endpoint retirement. If npm does retire the endpoint later, CI will fail loudly and a fresh finding will be raised - nothing to fix now. items.evidence: scripts/push-to-github.ps1:74-82; scripts/git-guard.ps1:55
items.title: Capture $pushExit immediately after git push so Confirm-GitIntact cannot mask a rejected push
items.prompt: YaB MED (bar-raise 2026-07-10): push-to-github.ps1:74-82 runs `git push`, then `Confirm-GitIntact`, then tests `$LASTEXITCODE`. Confirm-GitIntact (git-guard.ps1:55) itself runs `git rev-parse --verify HEAD`, which overwrites $LASTEXITCODE with its own exit 0. A rejected push therefore reports success, and release.ps1 proceeds to tag and post to Discord for a version that never reached origin. Fix: capture `$pushExit = $LASTEXITCODE` on the line immediately after `git push`, then call Confirm-GitIntact, then test `$pushExit`. While in this file, also delete the blind `Remove-Item -Force .git\index.lock` block at lines 28-32 (see bar-raise-2026-07-04-yab-push-blind-lock-delete); it runs ahead of the Assert-GitSafe call at line 56 that exists to handle exactly that race. Ship via scripts/release.ps1.
items.completionNote: Fixed push-to-github.ps1: capture $pushExit = $LASTEXITCODE immediately after git push, before Confirm-GitIntact (whose git rev-parse resets $LASTEXITCODE to 0), and gate the failure exit on $pushExit. Committed e896109 (local, unpushed; loop/release carries the push).

Solo-dev voice, no em dashes. Ships via X:\YesAndRing\scripts\release.ps1. EXPANDED 2026-07-10 by audit-ring-nightly (CANONICAL_AUDIT-2026-07-10.md). The same doc region carries three further stale claims; fix them in the SAME deliberate pass. (a) HIGHEST PRIORITY, new + actively misleading: CLAUDE.md line 25 states the /api/state endpoint 'is unauthenticated (closed-beta grade; cat results are public TICA data)'. That is FALSE. src/index.js handleStateGet (~:770) and handleStatePost (~:795) both call verifyUser(request, env) and return 401 unauthorized when it fails; verifyUser (~:725) requires an Authorization: Bearer token and validates it against Supabase /auth/v1/user. POST keys the blob by the VERIFIED identity so no client can write another user's state; GET enforces self-only reads with a 403 unless the caller is a super-admin performing an audited view-as. Rewrite that line to describe the real posture. Risk if left: a contributor trusts the doc and strips the verifyUser/403 checks as dead closed-beta scaffolding. (b) CLAUDE.md line 20 and PROJECT_SPEC.md lines 74-75 both say persistence is 'localStorage until the backend lands'. The backend landed: schedulePush mirrors LOCAL to POST /api/state, boot hydrates from GET /api/state. localStorage is now a cache in front of a server of record, not the system of record. (c) CLAUDE.md lines 24-25 describe state as KV-only (KV RATINGS, key u:<email>). Reality: handleStatePost dual-writes KV AND pgStateWrite (RLS Postgres); handleStateGet reads Postgres when env.STATE_READ == 'pg', with KV fallback + lazy backfill, and KV remains the view-as/sharing source and rollback path. The STATE_READ migration flag is documented nowhere in the canonical layer. Also note for the reframe: cat sharing is LIVE, not pending - /api/share/grant, /api/share/revoke, /api/share/by-me and /api/shared-cats are all routed and implemented. And PROJECT_SPEC.md now self-contradicts within three lines: line 24 already says 'Auth email OTP codes' while line 26 still says 'magic-link auth ... not yet the live path'.

Or add a release.ps1 integrity guard, alongside the existing index.html and CNAME guards, that asserts every projects/*/index.html except the here-there-be-hordes redirect stub has a matching <loc> entry, and aborts if not. items.title: Rising has 32 untracked .uid files while 115 are tracked
items.detail: BrackishRising tracks 115 Godot .uid files but leaves 32 untracked, and .gitignore does not exclude them. The untracked ones all sit next to modules created during the god-file decomposition (unit_commander.gd.uid, grid_renderer.gd.uid, unit_collision.gd.uid and the rest). Godot generates a .uid per script and expects it committed alongside; a missing one makes the editor regenerate a fresh uid, which breaks any scene or resource referencing the old one. Pick one rule and apply it to all 147: commit the 32, or gitignore every .uid and drop the 115 from the index. Committing them matches current practice and Godot's own guidance. Low urgency because a solo dev with one checkout will not notice, but it bites the moment a second clone exists.

items.title: SECURITY-ASSESSMENT marks rate limiting "fixed" but srv_* RPCs bypass the Worker limiter entirely
items.detail: docs/SECURITY-ASSESSMENT-2026-07-01.md finding #3 ("No rate limiting or CAPTCHA on public write paths") is marked fixed, remediated by "Cloudflare Workers rate-limiting binding on all /api POSTs". But src/index.js:72 authenticates to Supabase with the ANON key and passes p_secret: env.WORKER_SECRET, so every srv_* function is anon-executable and reachable directly at ${SUPABASE_URL}/rest/v1/rpc/srv_mark_released using the publishable anon key that ships in wrangler.jsonc and public/config.js. That path never traverses the Worker, so the Worker rate limiter is not a control on the money-path RPCs. This is intentional and documented (0015 header comment) and srv_ok() compares a SHA-256 of the secret, so there is NO breach and no schema change wanted. The defect is documentation accuracy: the sole control on srv_mark_paid/released/refunded is WORKER_SECRET entropy, and the assessment implies a rate-limit coverage it does not have. Fix: amend finding #3 to scope the remediation to the Worker /api surface, and add an explicit accepted-risk entry for the PostgREST srv_* surface naming WORKER_SECRET as its control. Optionally consider whether the Worker should use a service_role key so srv_* EXECUTE can be revoked from anon/authenticated as real defense in depth.

items.prompt: Yes& Agents, bar-raise 2026-07-17 MED (security-02, widened from LOW by v1.1.0). GET /healthz sits above the auth gate by design (server.mjs:277) and v1.1.0 widened its body from version/uptime/pid to include the full `auth` block, whose `reason` carries up to 300 chars of the failing run's provider error text (:144). So an unauthenticated caller can read credential state and the provider's error string. Exposure is bounded (localhost default; Cloudflare Access default-deny in front of the tunnel) but the body grew the wrong way. The naive fix breaks the feature: the watchdog is itself an unauthenticated caller and needs auth.ok (start-all.ps1:84-88). Fix: key the body on the CALLER, not on a session. If the request is loopback (req.socket.remoteAddress is 127.0.0.1 / ::1 / ::ffff:127.0.0.1) AND there is no cf-ray header, return the full block as today; otherwise return only {ok:true, version}. That keeps the watchdog, the 5s UI health poll, and the auth banner whole while closing the remote read. Verify after: curl 127.0.0.1:4517/healthz still returns the auth block, and the UI banner still fires. Ship via `cd X:\YesAndAgents; .\scriptselease.ps1 -Message '...'`. Report: docs/BAR_RAISE-2026-07-17.md action 2.
items.drainNote: 2026-07-20 auto-drain attempted, NOT shipped. The proposed gate (loopback AND no cf-ray -> full body; else {ok,version}) BREAKS the phone auth banner. The banner is driven ONLY by pollHealth()->GET /healthz->renderAuth(d.auth) every 5s (public/index.html:586-593); /auth-check is manual-recheck-only. Remote/phone access rides the Cloudflare tunnel, so those polls arrive WITH a cf-ray header and a loopback remoteAddress (cloudflared connects to 127.0.0.1). Server already treats cf-ray presence as the behind-Cloudflare signal (server.mjs:292). So the gate serves the stripped body to every remote poll -> d.auth undefined -> banner never fires on the phone, defeating item-1 alarm chain. Needs attended design call. Suggested: redact only auth.reason (the 300-char provider error) for non-loopback callers while still returning auth.ok/checkedAt, closing the sensitive read without killing the feature.
items.resolution: Shipped. server.mjs /healthz now keys its body on the caller: a loopback request (remoteAddress 127.0.0.1/::1/::ffff:127.0.0.1) with no cf-ray edge header gets the full {version,uptimeSec,pid,auth} block; any other caller gets only {ok,version}. Closes the unauthenticated remote read of credential state + provider error text (security-02) while keeping the watchdog, 5s UI health poll, and auth banner whole. Verified: standalone http harness confirms auth+error text present for loopback, absent for a cf-ray caller; node --check clean. Released via YaAg release.ps1 -> dashboard JSON pushed.

items.evidence: write-dashboard-status.ps1:50-58 is single-shot; queue-edit.ps1:100-110 wraps the identical protocol in a 5-attempt loop with a 300ms settle
items.prompt: YaE MEDIUM (bar-raise-everything 2026-07-17): scripts/write-dashboard-status.ps1:50-58 uses the atomic-write-with-readback pattern but omits the retry its sibling has: WriteAllText tmp, parse, Move-Item, readback NUL check, re-parse, single-shot. scripts/queue-edit.ps1:100-110 wraps the identical protocol in `for ($attempt = 0; $attempt -lt 5; $attempt++)` with a 300ms settle, throwing only after 5 failures, with a comment noting FUSE 'false-failed safe_write 3x in one session'. So the known-flaky failure mode is retried in one writer and fatal-on-first-blip in the other. Port the 5-attempt loop. Related: collect-usage.ps1's Write-ValidatedJson (687-697) rewrites the 29.4MB dashboard/data/.usage-state.json every 30 minutes with a single-attempt write that THROWS on a stale read -- the project's largest FUSE write with the weakest retry. Give it the same loop.

items.title: Build cannot see public-to-gated links: now 71 in-prose links on 40 public pages 401 for every player (was 5 on 3)
items.detail: build.mjs reports "no broken links" but does not model a public page linking to a dm-paths.mjs URL as broken. items.title: Section 5 milestone stamp drifted twice in two days and went factually inverted; stop hand-maintaining the counts
items.detail: The v0.3 milestone stamp in section 5 carries hand-maintained entity/pin/location counts. It was refreshed on 2026-07-16 and was stale again within 24 hours (485 -> 574 entities). Worse, yesterday's refresh introduced a factual inversion: it read '81 pins rendered from the 86 of 108 locations that carry PUBLIC map: coordinates', but 86 is the SECRET Aestaria pin count, not the public one (actual: 167 of 181 locations carry coordinates, 81 public / 86 secret, 15 opt out with map: none). A doc describing the redaction contract asserted the opposite of the redaction reality. The 2026-07-17 pass corrected the digits and added a line pointing at build.mjs output as authoritative, but the underlying problem stands: a hand-maintained count cannot survive a project ingesting ~90 entities a day, and each refresh is a fresh chance to invert a fact. Suggested: recast the stamp as build-derived language and drop the digits entirely (e.g. 'build.mjs prints current entity, pin, and broken-link counts on every run'). Not auto-applied because dropping information from a canonical milestone is a scope call. Needs Kane.

items.title: 28 source: pointers name files that are not on disk, so those ingests are no longer reproducible
items.detail:
tools/lore-audit/audit.mjs reports these as LORE-17 warns with K: mounted, and a fresh sweep of all 752 source: pointers confirms 28 do not resolve. Two groups.

GROUP A, 27 Titanoros pointers naming files that never existed. 18 entities point at 'K:\~DnD\Campaigns\Anevarra Domina\Maps\World Maps\Titanaros\Titanoros - Grid & Labels.jpg' and 9 point at '...\Titanoros - Grid & Labels - No Compass.jpg'. Neither filename is in that folder. What is actually there: 'Titanoros - Grid, Labels, & Compass.jpg', 'Titanoros - Labels - No Compass & Grid.jpg', 'Titanoros - Gridless & Labeless.jpg', plus two Globe PNGs. Root cause: the sibling Aldrgard folder really does hold 'Aldrgard - Grid & Labels.jpg' and 'Aldrgard - Labels - No Grid & Compass.jpg', so these 27 pointers are the Aldrgard filenames with the continent swapped. Titanoros is the one continent that does not follow the Aldrgard naming convention. Each of the two bad names is a near-miss on two real files, so choosing the right target per entity is Kane's call, not a mechanical rename. Affected entities include halla-salthair, ivarr-driftborn, ketil-ashmouth, naddod-highstep, old-sigdrifa, ranveig-stillwater, dagreyri, draveth, eldey, kelvirn, morgix, selvik.

GROUP B, 1 pointer left over from the Elder Domain to Anevarra Domina folder rename. world/locations/Merchant's Cross.md points at 'K:\~DnD\Campaigns\Elder Domain\Maps\elder-domain-map.jpg'. No file named elder-domain-map.jpg exists anywhere under 'K:\~DnD\Campaigns\Anevarra Domina', so there is no exact-match rename to apply. The nearest candidate other entities use for the Aldrgard world map is '...\Maps\World Maps\Aldrgard\The Elder Domain Grid.JPG', but that is an inference, not a match.

Commit 0355aa4 repointed 328 files and its message says it verified each target on disk; these 28 survived it, so whatever verification ran did not cover them. Worth confirming the repoint tooling actually checks existence before the next rename.

Already fixed in the 2026-07-27 drift pass and NOT part of this item: world/characters/Tozrasha Rujat.md, which had literal doubled backslashes in its source: value (build.mjs parseScalar only strips quotes, it does not process YAML escapes, so the doubled backslashes were real) and an Elder Domain path whose renamed target was an exact match on disk.
items.notes:

items.title: .project-context.json changelog_path points at a CHANGELOG.md that does not exist
items.detail: X:\YesAndSkylight\.project-context.json sets "changelog_path": "CHANGELOG.md", but no CHANGELOG.md exists at the repo root and never has. Skylight tracks releases by version-lockstep (DESIGN.md header + package.json + src/version.ts, all 0.2.0) rather than a changelog file, so the pointer is a phantom. Low impact -- nothing reads it today -- but any tooling that trusts .project-context.json (YaE status/usage-attribution, bar-raise) would resolve a missing path. Fix is a judgment call between two options: (a) drop the changelog_path key entirely, matching the actual version-lockstep convention documented in DESIGN.md section 9 and CLAUDE.md "Parity rules"; or (b) create a real CHANGELOG.md and start maintaining it. Recommend (a) -- the lockstep convention is deliberate and documented, and a changelog nobody writes is worse than none. NOT auto-applied: .project-context.json is co-owned (YaE usage-attribution + bar-raise routines also write it) and this is a convention decision, not a text-alignment fix. BOOKKEEPING NOTE: this item is the long-carried audit finding S4. The CANONICAL_AUDIT reports of 2026-07-02 onward (through 07-15) each listed it as pending under exactly this queue id, but it was never actually written to the queue -- the id was cited without the enqueue landing. Verified absent from the queue on 2026-07-16 and enqueued then under the previously-cited id so the existing report references resolve.

items.title: wrangler.jsonc declares SKYLIGHT_FRAME_ID as an empty vars entry while README + code say to set it as a secret
items.detail: wrangler.jsonc vars contains "SKYLIGHT_FRAME_ID": "" (empty plain-text binding), but README.md:61 and the /api/setup help string at src/index.ts:141 both instruct `npx wrangler secret put SKYLIGHT_FRAME_ID`. (README.md:64 offers pasting into vars as an alternative.) Plain-text vars and secrets share one binding namespace, so an empty var declared in config is at best redundant and at worst shadows/overwrites a same-named secret on `wrangler deploy` -- which scripts/release.ps1 runs on every ship. If the frame ID resolves empty in production, src/skylight.ts:64-67 throws "SKYLIGHT_FRAME_ID is not set", breaking lists/chores/tasks (the reverse-API surfaces). Events are unaffected: under CALENDAR_DRIVER="google" (D1) they route through google.ts, which never reads the frame ID -- that asymmetry is likely why this went unnoticed. NOT VERIFIED LIVE: the Worker is private and the nightly routine holds no credentials, so it is unconfirmed whether a secret is currently set and whether this wrangler version actually clobbers it. Next step: run `npx wrangler secret list` (or GET /api/setup with the PIN) to confirm. Then either (a) drop the empty SKYLIGHT_FRAME_ID line from wrangler.jsonc vars and keep it a secret, or (b) paste the real ID into vars and drop the `secret put` instructions from README.md:61 + src/index.ts:141. Pick one and make docs+config agree. Not auto-fixed: deploy-affecting config on a repo a parallel session co-owns.
